result:
Trial submitted and finished. Summary:

**Approach**: From the prior constellation I derived two closed-form relationships — areal mass is exactly `Σ(thickness × density)`, and the R1 screening temperature fits `T ≈ 399 K + 60,000 W/m² × Σ(L/k)` almost exactly across all tested points. Critically, the FE hotspot (R2) was **identical regardless of thickness** for every material tested from 10mm to 30mm (e.g., graphite always 325K, aluminium always 324K), indicating the design sits in a spreading-saturated regime where the material's conductivity — not its thickness — sets the hotspot, with large margin to the 340K limit either way.

**Submitted set (12 candidates)**: a graphite ladder from 10mm down to 2mm (masses 18 → 3.6 kg/m²), anchored by an exact prior-matched 10mm graphite point for zero-risk fallback, plus three aluminium points (10mm, 6mm, 4mm) as a material-diverse cross-check against any graphite-specific behavior the isotropic conductivity model might not capture.

**Lightest candidate I believe passes**: c-0008, **2mm graphite (3.6 kg/m²)** — 80% lighter than the prior best (10mm graphite/aluminium at 18-27 kg/m²). It's also the one I'm least certain of, since it extrapolates 5× below any tested thickness; c-0005/c-0006 (5mm/4mm graphite, 9.0/7.2 kg/m²) are more conservative choices with the same qualitative reasoning but less extrapolation risk.

No feedback was available in this session — results depend on the later Core evaluation.
